basis: Craniosynostosis, limb defects and intellectual disability define disease. Eyelid dysmorphism (30-79%) lacks demonstrated functional injury; renal anomalies are 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent blepharophimosis/proptosis are described as dysmorphism without established functional injury; ophthalmoplegia is only 5-29%.

basis: Developmental impairment and sleep apnea define disease: central apnea 7/8, obstructive apnea 3/8. Skeletal involvement includes clubfeet in 2/5; GI symptoms lack intrinsic organ injury.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: sleep apnea defines the syndrome; obstructive airway dysfunction occurs in 3/8, alongside central apnea in 7/8.

basis: Skin and dental dysplasia characterize IP. Corneal opacity and seizures each occur in 30-79% by HPO, supporting ocular and neurologic involvement despite the broader definition's wording.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental abnormalities are characteristic ectodermal defects explicitly included in the definition; hypodontia and abnormal dental morphology occur in 30-79%.

basis: Muscular dystrophy from an inborn protein O-glycosylation defect. Cardiomyopathy is 5-29% by HPO; respiratory impairment reflects skeletal respiratory-muscle weakness.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this dystroglycanopathy is an inherited protein O-glycosylation disorder, supported by its ancestors, and therefore qualifies as an inborn metabolic disorder.

basis: Defective B-cell development causes antibody deficiency and reduced B-cell counts (2/2). Recurrent respiratory and ear infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: impaired B-cell development with reduced B-cell counts in 2/2 is a defining blood-cell defect, in addition to the immunodeficiency mechanism.

basis: Definition identifies neurodevelopmental, skeletal and cardiac abnormalities as characteristic. Hearing impairment is 30-79%; scoliosis/limb asymmetry are 5-29% but explicitly defining.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: body asymmetry with leg-length difference and scoliosis are explicitly characteristic in the definition; their HPO frequencies of 5-29% would not support involved alone.

basis: Retinal dystrophy and renal ciliopathy are core recessive IFT140 presentations. Skeletal dysplasia varies by subtype; isolated retinal forms occur and umbrella renal frequency is uncertain.

decisions.renal: primary: renal ciliopathy is a core, common presentation of recessive IFT140 disease, including Mainzer-Saldino syndrome; isolated retinal forms make umbrella prevalence uncertain.

basis: Respiratory-chain defect; brain atrophy/seizures, retinopathy and pulmonary arterial hypertension each reported in 1/1. Skeletal findings omitted at cap; sepsis is separate.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment, seizures and brain atrophy occur in 1/1; the concept is defined by complex IV deficiency rather than a specific neurologic syndrome.

basis: Microphthalmia, intellectual disability and limb malformations characterize disease. Renal/ureteral defects occur in 30-79%; dental/cleft and pinna anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability and microcephaly are characteristic components explicitly included in the syndrome definition and occur in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic limb malformations are explicitly included in the syndrome definition; syndactyly, camptodactyly and duplicated thumb phalanges each occur in 30-79%.

basis: Intellectual disability occurs in 6/6. Persistent bowel dysfunction with chronic constipation occurs in 3/3; joint contractures in 2/3. Fine/sparse hair alone is cosmetic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint contractures impair joint function in 2/3; broad digits are dysmorphic features rather than evidence that skeletal disease defines FG syndrome 3.
